featured_reviews.review_text:
​I had a terrible experience taking my mother for an eye check-up here. Dr. Rakshit is highly rude, egoistic, and lacks the basic empathy required of a healthcare professional.
​When I asked for a simple explanation of her diagnosis, he dismissively said, "Number aaya hai." When I asked for the details, he snapped, "Likhke diya hai padhlo" (It’s written, read it yourself). Most people cannot interpret clinical eye test abbreviations, yet he refused to provide any clarity. He even spoke about me to his nurse in Gujarati, assuming I wouldn’t understand, saying he didn’t want to explain anything to me.

Myopia, or short-sightedness, is rising rapidly among children across India. While a mild prescription may seem manageable, unchecked progression in childhood can lead to significantly higher prescriptions and a greater risk of serious eye conditions in adulthood.
Children with myopia see nearby objects clearly but struggle with distant ones. They may squint frequently, sit closer to screens, or seem inattentive during outdoor activities. Many parents discover the issue only during a school checkup. A family history of myopia, excessive near work, reduced outdoor time, and prolonged screen use are all known risk factors.
High myopia — prescriptions beyond minus 6 diopters — is associated with increased risk of retinal detachment, glaucoma, and macular degeneration later in life, making early intervention essential.
Today, myopia management extends beyond glasses. Specially designed contact lenses, low-dose atropine eye drops, and at least one hour of outdoor activity daily have all been shown to slow progression meaningfully.
At Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre in Virar West, Dr. Anand Jaypuriya emphasises early detection and personalised eye care, including comprehensive pediatric eye evaluations.
If your child squints frequently or struggles to see the board at school, an early eye examination can make a lasting difference. Contact Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre, Virar West, to book a checkup.

Many people notice small spots or cobweb-like shapes drifting across their vision, especially against a bright background. These are called floaters, and in most cases they are a natural result of ageing. Knowing when they require urgent attention, however, is important.
Floaters form when tiny clumps develop in the vitreous — the gel inside the eye — and cast shadows on the retina. Flashes of light occur when the vitreous pulls on the retina. While occasional floaters are usually harmless, a sudden increase in their number, new flashes, or a curtain-like shadow across the vision can signal retinal detachment — a serious condition requiring immediate evaluation.
Those with high myopia, a history of eye injury, or prior eye surgery carry greater risk. A dilated retinal examination by an eye specialist can determine whether the floaters are benign or linked to an underlying retinal problem. Retinal tears, if caught early, can be treated effectively with laser before they progress to detachment.
At Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre in Virar West, Dr. Anand Jaypuriya emphasises early detection and personalised eye care for retinal and vitreous conditions.
Do not ignore a sudden change in your vision. Contact Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre, Virar West, for a thorough retinal evaluation.

Most of us spend hours every day staring at screens — for work, study, and entertainment. What many people do not realise is that this prolonged screen use quietly strains the eyes in ways that accumulate over time.
Computer Vision Syndrome, also called digital eye strain, causes tired or burning eyes, blurred vision, headaches, and neck discomfort. The eyes must work harder than usual to focus on a screen, particularly in poor lighting or with glare. People with uncorrected refractive errors like myopia or astigmatism are at greater risk, and children attending online classes are increasingly affected.
Simple habits help considerably. Following the 20-20-20 rule — looking at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes — relaxes the eye muscles. Proper screen positioning, adequate room lighting, and a routine eye examination to check for any underlying prescription needs are equally important.
At Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre in Virar West, Dr. Anand Jaypuriya emphasises early detection and personalised eye care. If your eyes feel consistently strained or tired, a detailed evaluation can identify the cause and provide lasting relief.
Reach out to Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre, Virar West, and protect your eyes before the discomfort becomes a daily struggle.

Many people are aware of cataracts and glaucoma, but fewer know about Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD), a condition that affects the macula—the central part of the retina responsible for sharp vision. AMD is one of the leading causes of vision impairment in adults above 50 and can affect activities such as reading, driving, recognizing faces, and using mobile phones.

At Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre, Dr. Anand Jaypuriya emphasizes the importance of regular retinal examinations for early detection of age-related eye diseases.

Common symptoms include blurred central vision, difficulty reading, distortion of straight lines, or needing brighter light for routine tasks. While peripheral vision often remains unaffected, central vision can gradually decline if the condition progresses.

Risk factors include increasing age, smoking, high blood pressure, family history, and prolonged exposure to unhealthy lifestyle habits. Regular eye examinations can help identify early changes and allow timely intervention.

If you are over 50 and have noticed changes in your reading vision or central vision, a detailed retinal examination can help identify potential concerns before they significantly impact your quality of life.

One of the biggest misconceptions among diabetic patients is that eye examinations are only necessary when vision becomes blurry. In reality, diabetic retinopathy often develops silently and may not affect vision until significant retinal damage has already occurred.

The retina contains delicate blood vessels that can be affected by prolonged high blood sugar levels. Early changes may not cause any symptoms, making annual retinal screening one of the most important preventive steps for diabetic patients.

At Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre, Dr. Anand Jaypuriya recommends regular retinal evaluation for all diabetic patients regardless of age or visual complaints.

Early detection allows timely treatment and can significantly reduce the risk of vision loss. Maintaining blood sugar, blood pressure, and cholesterol levels also plays an important role in protecting retinal health.

If you have diabetes and have not had a retinal examination in the last year, now is the ideal time to schedule one.
